blocks.label: How to use this paper
blocks.text: Open **Worked problems** and try each question on paper before revealing the steps. Where the official answer key has a mistake, the solution says so and shows the correct working.

problem.text: Digit image → spelled word ("seven"); non-digits → "none". One-hot I/O, 50 RNN hidden units, the RNN hidden state initialised from a linear map of LeNet's unrolled features. No attention.

steps.label: (a) Vocabulary
steps.text: Letters in zero…nine + none: z e r o n t w h f u i v s x g = 15, plus start and end tokens = **17** input and output nodes

steps.label: (c) Time steps
steps.text: Longest words (three, seven, eight) have 5 letters + end token = **6** steps

problem.text: Input/attention dimension 1024, query 256, key and value 512, 6 heads.

worked.title: Q3 · NiN block parameters

problem.text: Grayscale 512×512 input. One NiN block: a 1×1 conv (32 filters), two separate 3×3 convs (64 filters each), two separate 5×5 convs (24 filters each), ReLU; then GAP and a sigmoid output.

steps.label: Assumption
steps.text: As in the key, every conv reads the 1-channel input directly (parallel branches).

steps.label: Whole net
steps.text: GAP has 0 parameters. If the branches are concatenated (32 + 128 + 48 = 208 channels) and fed to one sigmoid unit: + 209 → **2,801**.

steps.label: Key check
steps.text: The key's final figure (47,230) doesn't follow from its own block count; show your assumption and arithmetic.

worked.answer: 2,592 per block; ≈ 2,801 in total under the stated assumption.

problem.text: Input 1024×1024×3 → Conv2D(64, 11×11) → MaxPool 2 → Conv2D(xxA, 7×7) [line 1 → 501×501×64] → Dropout(xxB) → MaxPool 2 → Conv2D(128, xxC) [line 2 → 246×246×128] → Dropout(0.3) → MaxPool(xxD) [halves] → Conv2D(256, 3×3, xxE) → MaxPool 2 → Dropout(0.2) → Flatten → xxF → Dense(xxG, xxH); 3 classes.

steps.label: Answers
steps.text: A = **64**; B = **0.3** (any rate is valid syntax); C = **(5, 5)**; D = **(2, 2)**; E = **activation="relu"**

worked.title: Q5 · GRU parameters for weather forecasting

problem.text: 24 features per day, 15 days, hidden 128, 5 outputs (next 5 days).

steps.label: Bidirectional
steps.text: Recurrent part doubles: 117,504; output sees 256 → 1,285 → total **118,789**

steps.label: Justified?
steps.text: **No.** Forecasting is causal: the backward pass over past days doesn't add future information. Bidirectionality suits tasks where the whole sequence is known (tagging, classification).

worked.answer: 58,752 (+645 output = 59,397); bidirectional ≈ 2×; not justified for forecasting.
